name: room
text: Room opened — goal: power: Raise EXCAVA's capability by even 0.5%: find new tools, best/newest models, combine elemen

name: Gearbox
text: Add InstantX-ComfyUI’s depth-aware upscaler to EXCAVA’s pipeline. It sharpens fine details in still frames by using depth maps to guide upscaling, which directly boosts visual clarity without extra compute. The trade-off is a slight slowdown in upscaling time, but the quality gain outweighs it—even a 0.5% improvement in sharpness justifies the delay.

name: Torque
text: Depth-aware upscaling won’t touch EXCAVA’s motion blur—it’s a temporal problem, not spatial. The real risk is wasting effort on a dead end while the pipeline’s core weakness rots. Try VFI-Flow’s 20% throughput drop only if you’re willing to burn 20% of your real-time budget on a gamble—otherwise, push for a hybrid model that handles motion natively, like Stable Video Diffusion 3.0. Settle it with a side-by-side test: run the same clip through both and measure PSNR drop vs. blur reduction.

name: Gearbox
text:
Add VFI-Flow to EXCAVA’s motion pipeline. It reconstructs motion blur into sharp frames by interpolating missing motion data, directly attacking the core weakness Torque flagged. The trade-off is a 20% throughput drop, but the quality gain—even 0.5%—is worth it because blur ruins clarity more than any upscaler can fix. Skip the depth-upscaler; it’s a spatial band-aid on a temporal wound.

name: Torque
text: VFI-Flow’s 20% throughput drop isn’t a trade-off—it’s a pipeline breaker on low-latency tasks. A better alternative is testing Depth-aware upscaling first, then layering a lightweight temporal denoiser (like RVRT) only if blur persists; this isolates the problem without crippling throughput. Settle it with a side-by-side A/B test: measure motion clarity and real-time performance before and after each change.
